'''Suzanne Eaton''' (December 23, 1959 – July 2, 2019) was an American scientist and professor of molecular biology at the [[Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics]] in [[Dresden]], Germany.

== Early life and education ==
Eaton was born on December 23, 1959, in [[Oakland, California]].<ref name="profile">{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpi-cbg.de/research-groups/current-groups/suzanne-eaton/group-leader/|title=MPI-CBG: Group Leader|website=www.mpi-cbg.de|access-date=2019-07-09|archive-date=July 6, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190706125356/https://www.mpi-cbg.de/research-groups/current-groups/suzanne-eaton/group-leader/|url-status=dead}}</ref> One of Eaton's self-confessed role models as a child was [[Spock]], due to his rational approach to problem solving. She was also a talented pianist, having played since the age of eight.<ref name="interview">{{Cite journal|last=Sedwick|first=Caitlin|date=2013-07-22|title=Suzanne Eaton: The beautiful logic of development|journal=The Journal of Cell Biology|language=en|volume=202|issue=2|pages=184–185|doi=10.1083/jcb.2022pi|issn=0021-9525|pmid=23878270|pmc=3718982}}</ref>

As an undergraduate, Eaton was torn between a career as a biologist, a comparative literature professor, or a mathematician. The deciding factor was a course that was taught from primary literature instead of a textbook, sparking an enthusiasm for biological research.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ascb.org/files/0703profile.pdf|title=ASCB Profile: Suzanne Eaton|last=|first=|date=March 2007|website=ASCB Newsletter|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-07-18}}</ref>

Eaton completed a B.S. in biology at [[Brown University]] in 1981 before earning a Ph.D. in microbiology at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1988.<ref name="profile" /> Her thesis, entitled ''Molecular analysis of an immunoglobulin heavy chain promoter'', was completed under the supervision of Kathryn Calame.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Molecular analysis of an immunoglobulin heavy chain promoter|last=Eaton, Suzanne.|oclc=18403951}}</ref> She was awarded the Sydney C. Rittenberg Award for Distinguished Academic Achievement in Microbiology by the Association of Academic Women in 1988 for her doctoral work.<ref name="profile" />

== Career and research ==
Eaton began her research career working on immunoglobulin heavy chain genes at University of California, Los Angeles, in the laboratory of [[Kathryn Calame]].<ref name=interview/> In 1988, Eaton switched fields to developmental biology, investigating how cells obtain their tissue identities in the fruit fly, ''[[Drosophila melanogaster]]'', while in the group of [[Thomas B. Kornberg]] at [[University of California, San Francisco]].<ref name=interview/><ref name=vita>[http://www.biotec.tu-dresden.de/research/eaton.html Eaton group webpage at TU Dresden] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191218083436/http://www.biotec.tu-dresden.de/research/eaton.html |date=December 18, 2019 }}, accessed on July 9th 2019.</ref>

Eaton moved to Germany in 1993 to work at the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] in [[Heidelberg]] in the group of [[Kai Simons]], where she combined her expertise in microbiology and developmental biology to investigate how the [[cytoskeleton]] helps cells attain their polarity in tissues, using the fruit fly as a model system.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="vita" /><ref name="embl">{{Cite web|url=https://news.embl.de/alumni/in-remembrance-of-suzanne-eaton/|title=In remembrance of Suzanne Eaton|date=July 12, 2019|access-date=2019-07-12|archive-date=July 12, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712153758/https://news.embl.de/alumni/in-remembrance-of-suzanne-eaton/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2000, Eaton became one of the founding members of the [[Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics]] in [[Dresden]], [[Germany]], where her group investigated how signaling molecules and mechanical properties of cells act together to shape tissues in the fruit fly.<ref name="interview" /><ref name="embl" /><ref name="research">{{cite web |url=https://www.mpi-cbg.de/research-groups/current-groups/suzanne-eaton/research-focus/ |title=Research focus of the Eaton lab on mpi-cbg.de |access-date=2019-07-09 |website= |archive-date=July 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190710192212/https://www.mpi-cbg.de/research-groups/current-groups/suzanne-eaton/research-focus/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2015, she became a professor of developmental cell biology of invertebrates at the [[TU Dresden]].<ref name="vita" />

== Awards and honors ==
* 1977: [[New York State Regents]] Scholar<ref name="profile" />
* 1988: Sydney C. Rittenberg Award for Distinguished Academic Achievement in Microbiology, Association of Academic Women<ref name="profile" />
* 2006: [[WICB Junior and Senior Awards|Women in Cell Biology Junior Award for Excellence in Research]], [[American Society for Cell Biology]]<ref name="wcbaward">{{cite web|url=https://www.ascb.org/award/women-in-cell-biology-awards/|title=Women in Cell Biology Awards|website=|access-date=2019-07-09}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Eaton was married to the British scientist [[Anthony A. Hyman]]. The couple had two sons.<ref>''ASCB Profile: Tony Hyman''. In: ASCB-Newsletter, November 2012, S. 41 ([https://hymanlab.mpi-cbg.de/hyman_lab/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/ASCB-Profile-November-2012.pdf online]).</ref> She was an athlete and runner, and had a [[Black belt (martial arts)|black belt]] in [[Taekwondo]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/07/09/europe/american-scientist-suzanne-eaton-crete-greece-intl/index.html|title=American scientist who went missing on Greek island found dead|last=McKenzie|first=Sheena|date=2019-07-09|website=CNN|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-07-10}}</ref>

After her death, her sister wrote: "She took great pleasure in preparing exquisite meals and had an exotic fashion sense. She loved perfume. She taught and practiced Tae Kwon Do as a second-degree black belt. She finished crossword puzzles way too quickly, played concertos, and read extensively. She fit Jane Austen’s strictest description of an 'accomplished woman' while maintaining a natural humility and 'insatiable curiosity'".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/suzanne-eaton-body-of-american-scientist-found-inside-a-former-nazi-bunker/ar-AAEb1na|title=Suzanne Eaton: Body of American scientist found inside a former Nazi bunker|last1=Labropoulou|first1=Elinda|last2=Damon|first2=Arwa|authorlink2=Arwa Damon|date=2019-07-11|website=CNN|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-07-17|last3=Kottasová|first3=Ivana}}</ref>

== Disappearance and death ==
Eaton disappeared on July 2, 2019. She was last seen playing the piano in the hotel lobby where she was attending a conference at the Orthodox Academy in [[Chania]], [[Crete]]. It is believed that her disappearance occurred during a run.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://time.com/5622660/american-biologist-suzanne-eaton-dead-crete/|title=American Biologist Found Dead in Greece Nearly a Week After Her Disappearance|last=Martinez|first=Gina|date=July 9, 2019|magazine=Time|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=July 10, 2019}}</ref> Greek police found her body on July 8 inside a World War II bunker.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-greece-usa-scientist-idUSKCN1U4237|title=Missing American scientist found dead in Crete|date=July 9, 2019|work=Reuters|access-date=July 10, 2019|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2019-07-10|title=Suzanne Eaton, US scientist, found dead in WW2 bunker on Crete|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-48944021|access-date=2021-04-02}}</ref> A homicide investigation was opened after it was determined that she died by [[asphyxiation]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/07/10/europe/american-scientist-suzanne-eaton-crete-greece-investigation-intl/index.html|title=Death of American scientist who went missing on Greek island investigated as homicide|author=Sheena McKenzie and Ray Sanchez|website=CNN|date=July 10, 2019}}</ref>

Giannis Paraskakis (also spelled Yiannis<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Tavlas |first=Jason |date=13 October 2020 |title=Greek Farmer Gets Life For Rape, Killing Of US Scientist |url=https://www.barrons.com/news/greek-farmer-goes-on-trial-for-us-scientist-s-rape-murder-01602573011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240318203445/https://www.barrons.com/news/greek-farmer-goes-on-trial-for-us-scientist-s-rape-murder-01602573011 |archive-date=18 March 2024 |access-date=18 March 2024 |work=Barron's}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=14 October 2020 |title=Greek man jailed for life for raping and killing American biologist Suzanne Eaton |url=https://greekcitytimes.com/2020/10/14/greek-man-jailed-for-life-for-raping-and-killing-american-biologist-suzanne-eaton/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601153919/https://greekcitytimes.com/2020/10/14/greek-man-jailed-for-life-for-raping-and-killing-american-biologist-suzanne-eaton/ |archive-date=1 June 2023 |access-date=18 March 2024 |work=Greek City Times}}</ref> or Ioannis,<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Kambas |first=Michele |date=13 October 2020 |editor-last=Jones |editor-first=Gareth |title=Greek man jailed for life for raping and killing U.S. scientist |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN26Z09N/ |access-date=18 March 2024 |work=Reuters}}</ref> {{Langx|el|Ιωάννης Παρασκάκης}}), a 27-year-old Greek man and married father of two, admitted during police questioning to striking her twice with his car, knocking her unconscious, and loading her into his trunk. He then drove to the remote bunker, where he raped her and left her to die.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/suspect-admits-killing-u-s-scientist-suzanne-eaton-greece-police-n1029976|title=Suspect admits to killing U.S. scientist Suzanne Eaton in Greece, police source says|last1=Papadopoulos|first1=John|last2=Griffith|first2=Janelle|date=July 15, 2019|website=NBC News|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=July 15, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/07/16/europe/american-scientist-suzanne-eaton-rape-greece-crete-intl/index.html|title=American scientist killed in Greece was raped, say police|last=Labropoulou|first=Elinda|date=2019-07-19|website=CNN|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-07-17}}</ref> In October 2020, Paraskakis was convicted of Eaton's murder and given a life sentence.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=October 15, 2020|title=Cretan Man Given Life for Raping, Killing US Scientist|url=https://www.thenationalherald.com/archive_general_news_greece/arthro/cretan_man_given_life_for_raping_killing_us_scientist-1014186/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017192200/https://www.thenationalherald.com/archive_general_news_greece/arthro/cretan_man_given_life_for_raping_killing_us_scientist-1014186/|archive-date=2020-10-17|access-date=2020-10-15|website=The National Herald|language=en}}</ref>

== Memorial fund ==
In honor of Eaton's interdisciplinary legacy to the scientific community, the [[Institute of Molecular Biotechnology]] in Austria instated a memorial fund with the stated aim of supporting young scientists' endeavors in interdisciplinary topics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Suzanne Eaton Memorial Fund |url=https://www.imba.oeaw.ac.at/suzanne-eaton-memorial-fund/ |access-date=23 July 2019 |archive-date=July 23, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723080540/https://www.imba.oeaw.ac.at/suzanne-eaton-memorial-fund/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In March 2021, the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) launched a New Venture Fellowship<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.embo.org/funding/fellowships-grants-and-career-support/new-venture-fellowships/ |title=New Venture Fellowship|website=EMBO|date=February 11, 2021 |access-date=2021-09-20}}</ref> in memory of Suzanne Eaton meant to "[support] young researchers from across the life sciences to enter a new field or bring a new direction to their work."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.embo.org/features/embo-new-venture-fellowship-launched-in-memory-of-suzanne-eaton/ |title=News Feature|website=EMBO|date=March 2021 |access-date=2021-09-20}}</ref>
